correctness.rationale: For every polygon with at least five vertices, prescribed nonadjacent ear tips are simultaneously deletable and counted by a Catalan completion number. The exact sign-product expansion over independent subsets has counting multiplicities. Catalan valuation and binary digit-sum subadditivity force all contributions of degree at least two into the next power of two. The degree-one term vanishes at this modulus for odd polygon sizes; for even sizes it has the exact base valuation and parity controlled by the frequency cardinality. Character diagonalization yields exact determinant valuation and the even-size rank bound. The standalone checker independently enumerated all polygon triangulations of five through eleven vertices and matched all 4,064 Walsh coefficients; all-frequency modular tests cover five through eighteen vertices. Finite testing does not replace the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The motivated question is parity-character recovery of complete original-boundary ear profiles, which is distinct from aggregate ear counting and spatial covariance. A natural infinite Catalan family has exactly determined all-frequency 2-adic valuations for every odd order despite infinitely many even Catalan counts; in every even order precisely half the characters occupy the sharp smallest dyadic stratum. The exact determinant valuation/rank obstruction are meaningful Fourier invariants, without claiming a full even-order singularity classification or general downstream application.
